# MLOps test fixtures — synthetic data

**Everything in this directory is synthetic. It is not evidence about the real
model, and it must never be used to fit a shipped calibration map.** A map fitted
on these rows would be a fabricated artifact, which is exactly what
`scripts/mlops/calibration.py::validate` and `Models/calibration/` exist to stop.

They are generated by `python scripts/tests/make_mlops_fixtures.py` (seed
`20260917`, stdlib `random` only), so `--check` reproduces them byte for byte.

| File | What it is | Why it exists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `synthetic_predictions.csv` | 400 forecasts: 20 districts × 2 horizons × 10 weekly issue dates, with an overconfident score (`0.5 + (p−0.5)·1.6`) and ~12 % hazard-class confusion | Calibration and verification code needs data with *known* properties; the real archive has no outcomes joined to predictions yet |
| `synthetic_outcomes.json` | 231 events drawn from the latent process, plus one landslide (a class the model does not predict), one event that predates its forecast, and one beyond a 7-day horizon | Exercises every bucket in the join — matched, unknown, near-miss, out-of-vocabulary |
| `reference_run.csv` | 300 published rows in the **legacy** `om_*` schema (mislabelled units, horizon totals) | Drift must convert before comparing |
| `current_run.csv` | The same weather in the **canonical** schema, with a changed precipitation regime on the last 30 rows | A correct conversion reports temperature/wind as stable and precipitation as shifted |

The two run files describe the same weather by construction. That is deliberate: a
unit conversion that is wrong in either direction turns "stable" into a headline
drift index, so the drift tests fail loudly instead of quietly reporting noise.

## What the synthetic set can and cannot support

* **Can**: exercise the matcher's buckets, the isotonic/Platt fits, the refusal
  rules, the registry, PSI, and the CLI paths end to end.
* **Cannot**: make any claim about the deployed model. The numbers a run produces
  from these files are *properties of the fixture*, which is why
  `Models/REGISTRY.json` and `docs/MODEL_CARD.md` never quote them as model results.

`absence_means_no_event=True` is legitimate here and only here: this fixture was
generated from a complete latent truth, so "no event recorded" really does mean "no
event". Real archives are not complete, which is why the default is `unknown`.
